BillHeading.Sponsors: House Transportation (originally sponsored by Representatives Ortiz-Self and Kloba)
BillHeading.BriefDescription: Requiring the transportation commission to conduct a study of discounted tolls and other similar programs for low-income drivers.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing discounted toll rates to certain individuals on certain tolled facilities; and creating a new section.

BillSectionHeader.P: (1) The transportation commission shall conduct a study of discounted tolls and other similar programs, for low-income drivers, that are provided by other states, countries, or other jurisdictions. The transportation commission may contract with a consultant to conduct all or a portion of this study.

BillSection.P: (2) In conducting the study, the transportation commission shall consult with both the department of transportation and the department of social and health services.
(3) The transportation commission shall, at a minimum, consider the following issues when conducting the study of discounted tolls and other similar programs, for low-income drivers:
(a) The benefits, requirements, and any potential detriments to the users of a program;

(b) The most cost-effective way to implement a program given existing financial commitments, shared cost requirements across facilities, and technical requirements to execute and maintain a program; and
(c) The implications of a program for tolling policies, revenues, costs, operations, and enforcement.

(4) The transportation commission shall provide a report detailing the findings of this study and recommendations for implementing a discounted toll or other appropriate program in the state of Washington to the transportation committees of the legislature by December 1, 2019.
